title: The experienced trader's mug
hook: Should market experience change the gap between buying and selling prices?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast ownership valuation across experience groups rather than asserting a universal endowment ratio.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast ownership valuation across experience groups rather than asserting a universal endowment ratio.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy valuation table, a buyer offers €5 while an owner asks €8. What is the sell-to-buy ratio? Toy inputs A=[5, 8]; B=[6, 6].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[1.6, 5, 8], [1, 6, 6]]. Labels: Sell/buy, Buy €, Sell €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The two elicited prices define a gap for this table. The comparison has no gap, showing why one universal ownership multiplier would be a stronger claim than the arithmetic supports. Neither case is a measured participant sample.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Buy €=6, Sell €=6. What is Sell/buy? Answer: 1.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Buy €=6, Sell €=6. What is Sell/buy?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 1. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Experienced sports-card dealers showed little endowment effect (List, 2003).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast ownership valuation across experience groups rather than asserting a universal endowment ratio.
